title: Short Stuff: Sleeping On It
summary: Short Stuff episode on "sleeping on it," the idea that sleep or unconscious thought helps people make better decisions on complex, important choices. The hosts cover research suggesting sleep helps organize and consolidate memories and connect new and old information, and that unconscious thought (stepping away and doing something else) can produce balanced decisions by reducing conscious biases and overthinking. They discuss a study by Dijksterhuis on choosing apartments, where unconscious thinkers chose better than conscious thinkers, and a follow-up suggesting experts also decide worse under snap pressure. They close by noting that stepping away from stressful immediacy helps, and debate whether high-pressure jobs allow time to sleep on decisions. Josh mentions a future long-form episode on napping. The episode ends with an ad read for iHeartRadio-produced podcasts.

segments.title: Opening and source credits
segments.summary: Josh introduces the short episode and credits sources including WebMD, the NIH, and a Live Science guest post by John Grohol. The hosts joke about the spelling and pronunciation of Grohol's name and introduce the everyday experience of sleeping on a decision.

segments.title: Why sleep helps decisions
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how sleep helps with complex decisions, not trivial ones. Research suggests sleep organizes memories and connects new information to old, consolidating neural pathways so people gain clarity. Matthew Walker of UC Berkeley is cited on sleep aiding learning.

segments.title: Napping teaser and break
segments.summary: Chuck mentions a daily nap habit and Josh says napping will be the topic of a future long-form episode. They take a break, and the hosts joke about the nap.

segments.title: Unconscious thought versus conscious thought
segments.summary: The hosts explain research suggesting that unconscious thought, such as stepping away and doing something else, can produce decisions as good as sleeping on them. Grohol is cited as pointing out unconscious thought is a different mode of thinking, not zoning out.

segments.title: Overthinking and biases
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how overthinking lets biases creep in, and how unconscious thought lets biases fade so the important factors stand out. The snickerdoodle cookie example illustrates a bias toward a desirable but irrelevant option.

segments.title: Apartment study and expert decisions
segments.summary: The hosts describe a study by Dijksterhuis in which participants chose among apartments after conscious or unconscious thought, with unconscious thinkers choosing better. A follow-up found experts making snap decisions did worse than non-experts who had time to sleep on it or use unconscious thought.

segments.title: Stress, immediacy, and high-pressure jobs
segments.summary: The hosts argue that stepping away removes the stress of immediacy and leads to better decisions unless someone is under real duress. They debate whether high-pressure management jobs allow time to sleep on decisions.

segments.title: Sign-off and iHeartRadio credit
segments.summary: The hosts joke about starting a company called Sleep On It and close the short episode with the production credit for iHeartRadio.
